title: The discovery that routed to ghosts
blurb: Expired instances stayed routable and deploy swaps collided.
prompt: Traffic kept landing on dead instances for minutes after a crash, and a deploy briefly had two instances claiming the same identity with different metadata. The model-generated draft refreshes TTL without metadata and returns instances by registration rather than health. Review it, fix it, and prove membership is heartbeat- and health-true.
aiNote: The draft renews a heartbeat with a bare EXPIRE, so a replaced instance's stale metadata lives on as long as anything renews it, and it registers the replacement before deregistering the original, so two addresses occupy one identity during a deploy window.
testIdea: Stop heartbeats and assert the instance leaves the routable set within the interval bound; register a replacement while the old one is live and assert one address per identity; probe-fail an instance and assert it is excluded and later readmitted.
followUps: How many missed heartbeats mean dead?
Should probes be centralized or per-caller?
What identity do rolling deploys need?
